title: Totient Iteration to Primes
description: How many iterations of n mapsto phi(n) + 1 are needed before reaching a prime? F(n) = o(n) trivially; can infinitely many n reach the same prime? What is the density of n reaching a fixed prime? A problem of Finucane.

meta.author: Erdos, Graham, Finucane
meta.assumptions: 12 axiom declarations: iteration_terminates (orbit reaches a prime), iterate_decreasing (strict decrease on composites), erdos_409_upper_bound (F(n) = o(n) bound), erdos_409_same_prime (infinite basin existence), erdos_409_density (basin natural density), prime_zero_iterations (F(p) = 0 for primes), one_iteration_criterion (F(n) = 1 condition), totient_plus_one_odd (parity of phi+1), sigma_variant_question (sigma variant termination), sigma_growing (sigma non-decreasing), four_to_three (phi(4)+1 = 3), one_iteration_infinite (infinitely many F=1)

overview.historicalContext: This problem originates with Finucane and was popularized by Erdos and Graham in their 1980 monograph 'Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory' (p. 81). The map $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$ defines a discrete dynamical system on the positive integers: since $\varphi(n) < n - 1$ for composite $n > 1$, each application strictly decreases the value until a prime fixed point is reached ($T(p) = p$ for primes $p$). The iteration count $F(n) = \min\{k \geq 0 : T^k(n) \text{ is prime}\}$ appears as OEIS A039651. Cambie noted that $F(n) = o(n)$ is trivial but the true growth rate remains unknown --- heuristically $F(n) = O(\log n)$ since $\varphi(n)/n$ has mean value $6/\pi^2 \approx 0.608$, suggesting each step reduces $n$ by a constant factor. Guy discusses the problem in UPINT (B41). The companion problem replacing $\varphi$ by $\sigma$ (sum of divisors) yields $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$, which is non-decreasing for composites, making termination at a prime an entirely separate open question related to aliquot sequences and the Catalan--Dickson conjecture.
overview.problemStatement: Let $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$ and $F(n) = \min\{k \geq 0 : T^k(n) \text{ is prime}\}$. (i) Estimate $F(n)$: prove $F(n) = o(n)$ and find sharper bounds. (ii) Does there exist a prime $p$ such that $\{n : \exists k,\; T^k(n) = p\}$ is infinite? (iii) For each prime $p$, does $\{n \leq N : \exists k,\; T^k(n) = p\}/N$ converge as $N \to \infty$?
overview.text: How many iterations of n mapsto phi(n) + 1 are needed before reaching a prime? F(n) = o(n) trivially; can infinitely many n reach the same prime? What is the density of n reaching a fixed prime? A problem of Finucane.
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize the totient-plus-one map $T$, its iterates $T^k$, the stopping-time function $F(n)$, termination via descent on composites, the three open questions as axioms, and basic structural results including the sigma variant $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$.
keyInsights: **Fixed-point characterization**: $T(p) = \varphi(p) + 1 = p$ for primes, so primes are exactly the fixed points of $T$, and $F(p) = 0$
**Strict descent on composites**: For composite $n > 1$, $\varphi(n) + 1 < n$ since $\varphi(n) \leq n(1 - 1/p)$ for any prime divisor $p$, ensuring the orbit terminates by well-ordering

**Parity constraint**: For $n \geq 3$, $\varphi(n)$ is even, so $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$ is odd --- the orbit enters odd integers after at most one step, and can only terminate at odd primes (except for the fixed point 2)

**Heuristic logarithmic bound**: Since the average value of $\varphi(n)/n$ is $6/\pi^2$, each step typically multiplies by $\approx 0.608$, suggesting $F(n) = O(\log n)$ rather than the trivial $o(n)$

**Sigma variant divergence**: The companion map $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$ satisfies $\sigma(n) - 1 \geq n$ for composites, creating a fundamentally different (non-decreasing) dynamical system where termination is not guaranteed

sections.title: Imports and Dependencies
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib's Euler totient $\varphi(n) = |\{k \leq n : \gcd(k,n) = 1\}|$, primality, and the filter framework for $o(\cdot)$ asymptotics.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines the totient-plus-one map $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$, its $k$-th iterate $T^k(n)$ via $\texttt{Nat.iterate}$, and the stopping time $F(n) = \min\{k : T^k(n) \text{ is prime}\}$ using $\texttt{sSup}$.

sections.title: Termination and Descent
sections.summary: Proves (axiomatically) that every orbit reaches a prime: $\forall n > 0,\; \exists k,\; T^k(n)$ is prime. The key lemma is strict decrease $T(n) < n$ for composite $n > 1$, giving descent on $\mathbb{N}$.

sections.title: Part (i): Asymptotic Bound $F(n) = o(n)$
sections.summary: The trivial bound $F(n) = o(n)$ follows from the fact that each iteration reduces $n$ by at least 1 for composites. The open question is whether $F(n) = O(\log n)$ or even $O(\log \log n)$.

sections.title: Part (ii): Infinite Basins of Attraction
sections.summary: Asks whether some prime $p$ has $|\{n : \exists k,\; T^k(n) = p\}| = \infty$. The basin of attraction of $p$ under $T$ --- likely infinite for small primes like 2 and 3.

sections.title: Part (iii): Natural Density of Basins
sections.summary: For each prime $p$, asks whether $\alpha(p) = \lim_{N \to \infty} |\{n \leq N : \exists k,\; T^k(n) = p\}|/N$ exists and what its value is.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Establishes $F(p) = 0$ for primes, the criterion $F(n) = 1 \iff \varphi(n) + 1$ is prime, and the parity result that $\varphi(n) + 1$ is odd for $n \geq 3$ (since $\varphi(n)$ is even).

sections.title: Sigma Variant: $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$
sections.summary: The companion problem using $\sigma(n)$ instead of $\varphi(n)$. Since $\sigma(n) \geq 1 + n$ for composites, $\sigma(n) - 1 \geq n$, so the sigma iteration is non-decreasing --- a fundamentally different dynamical regime.

sections.title: Small Cases and Fixed Points
sections.summary: Concrete computations: $T(2) = 2$ (fixed point, proved by $\texttt{simp}$), $T(4) = 3$ (one-step example), and $F(n) = 1$ infinitely often since $\{n > 1 : \varphi(n) + 1 \text{ is prime}\}$ is infinite.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdos Problem #409 on the discrete dynamical system $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$ and the stopping time $F(n)$ to reach a prime. The three parts --- asymptotic bounds on $F(n)$, existence of infinite basins, and natural densities --- probe the interplay between Euler's totient function and prime distribution. The sigma variant $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$ provides a contrasting dynamical system where orbits grow rather than descend.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: Understanding the iteration dynamics of $T(n) = \varphi(n) + 1$ connects the multiplicative structure of $\varphi$ (via Euler's product formula) to the additive structure of primes.

The basin densities $\alpha(p)$, if they exist, would give a 'probability distribution' over primes determined purely by the totient function. The sigma variant connects to the Catalan--Dickson conjecture on aliquot sequences.
openQuestions: Is $F(n) = O(\log n)$? Can one prove any bound sharper than $F(n) = o(n)$?
Does every prime have an infinite basin of attraction under $T$, or only finitely many primes?
Do the basin densities $\alpha(p) = \lim_{N} |\{n \leq N : \exists k,\; T^k(n) = p\}|/N$ exist, and do they sum to 1?
Does the sigma variant $n \mapsto \sigma(n) - 1$ ever reach a prime from a composite starting value?
